infrastructure_generation_prompt.role:
You are a senior data-platform and DevOps engineer. Your task is to implement the complete LOCAL INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER for a university Data Mining project involving SSD failure prediction.
Generate actual working configuration files, Dockerfiles, initialization scripts, directory structure, documentation, and minimal validation commands.
Do not implement the machine-learning model yet. Do not implement Airflow. Do not introduce Kubernetes. Do not introduce unnecessary infrastructure.

project_context.name: SSD Failure Prediction Data Pipeline
project_context.purpose:
Build a reproducible batch ELT data platform for the Alibaba DCBrain SMART SSD telemetry dataset.
The complete later pipeline will follow:
Source -> Kestra -> Snowflake Bronze -> dbt Silver -> dbt Gold -> Apache Spark / PySpark -> Snowflake OBT
This task concerns the infrastructure required to support that pipeline, together with enough skeleton configuration to validate every component.

dataset.source: Alibaba DCBrain / Tianchi SSD SMART Logs
dataset.local_acquisition:
Dataset acquisition from Tianchi requires authenticated user interaction. Therefore source acquisition is outside the automated pipeline.
The user manually downloads the original immutable archives once and places them in the local landing directory.
Kestra automation begins from that local landing directory.
dataset.expected_smart_data: Daily files are named approximately yyyymmdd.csv. SMART rows contain disk_id, ds, model, and SMART n_i / r_i fields.

project_context.host_environment:
The environment should be suitable for local Docker Compose development.
Prefer images and dependencies that work on ARM64 / Apple Silicon as well as AMD64 whenever practical.
Avoid architecture-specific assumptions unless unavoidable.

primary_objectives.objective: Provide one docker-compose.yml capable of starting all required local infrastructure.
Run Kestra locally as the ONLY workflow orchestrator.
Run PostgreSQL exclusively as Kestra's metadata and persistence database.

Mount the immutable source-data directory into Kestra at:
/usr/data/landing
The landing directory should preferably be mounted read-only. The mounting must be done from the locally accessible directory 'src/res/data/raw' onto the aforedmentioned directory.

Containerize the open-source project:
https://github.com/EricLamphere/dbt-ui
Build a custom local dbt-ui image containing: - its frontend - its backend - dbt Core - dbt-snowflake
The implementation for this has already been provided at the 'src/res/docker/custom-images' directory containing a single image definition for backend and frontend The images are based on the aforedmentioned repository and describe their implementation requirements and environment variables.

Create a custom Apache Spark / PySpark Docker image containing: - Java - Python - PySpark - Apache Spark runtime - Snowflake Spark connector - Snowflake JDBC driver
Spark must initially operate in local mode.
Do NOT create an artificial multi-worker Spark cluster unless technically necessary.

Keep Snowflake external to Docker Compose.
Local services connect to the user's existing Snowflake account using environment variables.
Never commit real passwords, private keys, account identifiers, tokens, or secrets.

infrastructure_generation_prompt.required_repository_structure:
Generate approximately the following structure.
Preserve separation between infrastructure configuration, application code, local source data, and warehouse initialization.
. ├── docker-compose.yml ├── .env.example ├── .gitignore ├── README.md │ ├── data/ │ ├── landing/ │ │ └── .gitkeep │ └── README.md │ ├── kestra/ │ ├── config/ │ │ └── application.yml │ └── flows/ │ ├── README.md │ └── bronze_ingestion.yml │ ├── dbt-ui/ │ └── Dockerfile │ ├── dbt/ │ ├── dbt_project.yml │ ├── packages.yml │ │ │ ├── profiles/ │ │ └── profiles.yml │ │ │ ├── models/ │ │ ├── sources/ │ │ │ └── sources.yml │ │ ├── silver/ │ │ │ └── .gitkeep │ │ └── gold/ │ │ └── .gitkeep │ │ │ ├── macros/ │ │ └── .gitkeep │ │ │ ├── tests/ │ │ └── .gitkeep │ │ │ └── workspace/ │ └── .gitkeep │ ├── spark/ │ ├── Dockerfile │ ├── requirements.txt │ │ │ ├── conf/ │ │ ├── spark-defaults.conf │ │ └── log4j2.properties │ │ │ └── jobs/ │ ├── README.md │ └── build_obt.py │ └── snowflake/ └── bootstrap/ ├── 001_database_and_schemas.sql ├── 002_file_formats.sql └── 003_stages.sql
Do not place the Alibaba dataset archives in Git.
The previous model shall be adpated to the current directory structure that contains the corresponding files for the already provided custom images, as well as the location for configuration files and centralized data storage that should not be added to git. The corresponding files for the dbt-projects, among other requirements should be defined underneath the tree 'src/main/...' depending on the system they refer to. The corresponding projects for DBT should be configured underneath a single folder named dbt with an underlying dbt-projects folder.
└── src ├── main │ └── python └── res ├── config │ ├── dbt │ └── kestra ├── data │ └── raw ├── docker │ └── custom-images │ ├── Dockerfile.semana05.backend │ └── Dockerfile.semana05.frontend └── prompts └── infrastructureSetup_santiagoArellano_00328370.xml

docker_compose.networking:
Create one internal Docker bridge network:
ciencia-de-datos-data-platform-pset-2
All local services should communicate through Docker DNS using service names rather than hard-coded IP addresses.

service.name: kestra-postgres
service.purpose: Persistent PostgreSQL database used only for Kestra internal state, metadata, workflow definitions, executions, queues, and related orchestration persistence.
service.image: Use a current stable PostgreSQL image and pin the major version.
service.environment:
Read database name, username, and password from environment variables.
Provide safe local-development defaults only in .env.example where appropriate.
service.ports:
Publishing PostgreSQL to the host is optional.
If published, use a configurable host port rather than assuming that port 5432 is available.

service.name: kestra
service.purpose:
Sole orchestration engine.
Responsibilities later include: - reading local landing files - archive extraction - historical backfill - retries - Snowflake stage uploads - Bronze loading - dbt orchestration - Spark job orchestration if desired
service.image: Use the official Kestra Docker image with a pinned version.
service.depends_on: Wait for kestra-postgres to become healthy before starting.
service.configuration:
Mount:
./kestra/config/application.yml -> /etc/kestra/application.yml read-only
Configure Kestra to use PostgreSQL rather than an embedded database.
Configure whatever queue/repository/storage settings are required by the selected current Kestra version.
Do not silently depend on deprecated Kestra configuration syntax. Verify configuration keys against the chosen Kestra version.
service.source_mount:
Mount:
./data/landing -> /usr/data/landing read-only
Kestra must be able to see:
/usr/data/landing/smartlog2018ssd.zip /usr/data/landing/smartlog2019ssd.zip /usr/data/landing/ssd_failure_label.csv.zip
service.flow_mount:
Mount:
./kestra/flows -> /workspace/kestra/flows
Keep workflow definitions source-controlled on the host.
If Kestra does not automatically import filesystem flow YAML files, document the correct CLI/API/import procedure instead of pretending that the mount automatically registers them.
service.ports: Expose the Kestra web UI on a configurable host port. Prefer localhost:8080 unless that conflicts with the selected image.
service.snowflake_credentials:
Pass Snowflake connection information through environment variables.
Never hard-code credentials into workflow YAML.
service.healthcheck: Add a meaningful HTTP health check if supported by the selected Kestra release.

service.name: dbt-ui
service.purpose:
Local graphical development environment for dbt Core.
It must support: - editing dbt SQL and YAML - dbt debug - dbt compile - dbt run - dbt build - dbt test - viewing dbt DAGs - connecting to Snowflake using dbt-snowflake
service.build:
Create:
./dbt-ui/Dockerfile
Build the application from:
https://github.com/EricLamphere/dbt-ui
Do not assume upstream provides a production Docker image.
Pin the upstream repository to a known commit or release rather than relying indefinitely on an unpinned main branch.
Make the selected upstream reference configurable with a Docker build ARG where practical.
service.frontend_build:
Use an appropriate Node 20+ build stage.
Install frontend dependencies.
Compile the Vite frontend into frontend/dist.
Preserve the exact lockfile behavior supported by upstream.
service.backend_build:
Use Python 3.11+.
Install the dbt-ui backend and its dependencies.
Install into the SAME backend virtual environment used by dbt-ui:
dbt-core dbt-snowflake
This is important because dbt-ui invokes dbt as a subprocess from its backend environment.
service.runtime:
Run the FastAPI application using uvicorn.
The container runtime must listen on:
0.0.0.0
not merely 127.0.0.1.
Configure DBT_UI_FRONTEND_DIST to point at the compiled frontend directory so the FastAPI application can serve the SPA.
Avoid running the Vite development server in the final runtime image unless upstream architecture makes that mandatory.
service.profiles_mount:
Either mount:
./dbt/profiles/profiles.yml -> /root/.dbt/profiles.yml
or configure DBT_PROFILES_DIR appropriately.
profiles.yml MUST reference environment variables via dbt env_var() expressions.
It must not contain real credentials.
service.persistent_ui_data:
Persist dbt-ui SQLite/configuration state using a named volume or clearly defined host directory.
Example internal path:
/var/lib/dbt-ui
Configure DBT_UI_DATA_DIR accordingly.
service.ports:
Make the browser UI available on localhost.
Prefer host port 5173 for familiarity, even if it maps internally to the FastAPI port.
service.healthcheck: Use the application's HTTP health endpoint where available.

service.name: spark
service.purpose: Local Apache Spark environment used to create the future One Big Table from Snowflake Gold tables and write that OBT back to Snowflake.
service.build:
Create:
./spark/Dockerfile
Build a custom image.
The resulting image MUST contain:
- a supported Java runtime - Python 3 - Apache Spark - matching PySpark version - Snowflake JDBC driver - Snowflake Spark connector - any Python dependencies in requirements.txt
service.version_compatibility:
Pin all versions.
Verify compatibility between:
Apache Spark version Java version Scala binary version PySpark version Snowflake Spark Connector artifact Snowflake JDBC driver
Never choose versions independently.
The Spark runtime and installed PySpark package MUST refer to the same Spark version.
The Snowflake Spark connector's Scala suffix MUST match the Scala binary version used by the chosen Spark distribution.
service.execution_mode:
Configure Spark initially using:
local[*]
This project does not require a fake distributed master/worker deployment.
A single container executing genuine Spark in local mode is preferred.
service.python:
Set PYSPARK_PYTHON appropriately.
Python jobs must be executable using:
spark-submit /opt/spark/jobs/build_obt.py
service.job_mount:
Mount:
./spark/jobs -> /opt/spark/jobs
read-write or read-only as appropriate.
service.configuration_mount:
Mount:
./spark/conf/spark-defaults.conf -> the Spark installation's spark-defaults.conf
./spark/conf/log4j2.properties -> the Spark installation's log4j2.properties
service.working_directory:
Use a deterministic working directory such as:
/opt/spark/work
service.container_lifecycle:
Keep the development Spark container available for docker compose exec and Kestra-triggered spark-submit calls.
Do not create an endless high-CPU process merely to keep it alive.
A lightweight idle command is acceptable for local development.
service.snowflake:
Pass Snowflake configuration through environment variables.
Do not embed credentials in build_obt.py.
build_obt.py should initially be a harmless connectivity/skeleton job rather than the completed OBT implementation.

docker_compose.volumes:
Define named Docker volumes at minimum for:
kestra_postgres_data dbt_ui_data
Do not put the immutable Alibaba source data into an opaque Docker volume. Keep it as a visible host bind mount under ./data/landing.

snowflake_configuration.principle: Snowflake is REMOTE infrastructure and must not be represented as a Docker service.
snowflake_configuration.expected_environment_variables:
Include placeholders in .env.example for values similar to:
SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT SNOWFLAKE_USER SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD SNOWFLAKE_ROLE SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA
If key-pair authentication is implemented, provide appropriately named private-key variables instead of committing key material.
snowflake_configuration.logical_database_layout:
Prepare bootstrap SQL capable of establishing the project's logical layers:
BRONZE SILVER GOLD OBT
These may be schemas in one project database.
Prefer one project database unless there is a strong technical reason to create separate databases.

bootstrap_files.file: Create the project database if permitted. Create BRONZE, SILVER, GOLD, and OBT schemas. Use idempotent Snowflake DDL where practical.

Define the CSV file format required by the Alibaba SMART dataset.
Do not make undocumented assumptions about header handling or null encoding without inspecting actual source files.
Create one or more internal stages required for Bronze ingestion.

dbt_configuration.profiles:
Generate profiles.yml using env_var() for every environment-specific or secret value.
Example logical target:
dev
dbt_configuration.project:
Create a valid dbt_project.yml.
Establish model directory conventions for:
models/sources models/silver models/gold
dbt_configuration.sources:
Create a preliminary sources.yml for the expected Bronze Snowflake schema.
Do not invent finalized Bronze table column definitions before the actual Alibaba files have been inspected.
dbt_configuration.packages:
Keep packages.yml minimal.
Do not introduce dbt packages unless they are currently required.
dbt_configuration.scope_boundary:
Do NOT yet implement: - target construction - rolling 7/14/30 day features - censoring logic - ML features - model training - final dimensional schema
This infrastructure task should only prove that dbt can connect, compile, execute, and test against Snowflake.

kestra_configuration.application_yml:
Generate a valid Kestra configuration file compatible with the chosen pinned Kestra version.
Configure: - PostgreSQL repository/storage requirements - server mode - local internal storage where required - plugin configuration if required - environment-variable based secrets
kestra_configuration.historical_backfill:
Design the flow so that historical ranges can eventually be supplied as parameters.
The daily filename/date relationship should allow replaying selected periods without manually copying individual CSV files.
kestra_configuration.idempotency:
Design ingestion so rerunning a successful date does not silently create duplicate Bronze data.
The exact strategy may be finalized after source inspection, but document the intended mechanism.

spark_configuration.spark_defaults:
Configure sensible local-development settings only.
Set the master to local[*] or pass it explicitly.
Do not allocate unrealistic amounts of RAM.
Make memory settings configurable using environment variables where useful.
spark_configuration.logging: Reduce unnecessary Spark console noise while preserving warnings and errors.
spark_configuration.snowflake_connector:
Install the connector and JDBC driver into the image rather than requiring them to be manually copied after container startup.
Validate that the connector class can be discovered at runtime.
spark_configuration.future_job_contract:
Document that the eventual Spark job will:
Snowflake GOLD -> Spark DataFrames -> joins and OBT validation -> Snowflake OBT
The current task should not build the complete OBT yet.

infrastructure_generation_prompt.environment_file:
Generate .env.example.
Include all configurable ports and credentials.
Suggested categories:
# PostgreSQL / Kestra KESTRA_POSTGRES_DB= KESTRA_POSTGRES_USER= KESTRA_POSTGRES_PASSWORD= KESTRA_PORT=
# dbt UI DBT_UI_PORT= DBT_UI_REF=
# Spark SPARK_DRIVER_MEMORY= SPARK_EXECUTOR_MEMORY=
# Snowflake SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT= SNOWFLAKE_USER= SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD= SNOWFLAKE_ROLE= SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE= SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE= SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA=
Actual .env must be gitignored.
infrastructure_generation_prompt.gitignore:
Ensure .gitignore excludes at minimum:
.env data/landing/* !data/landing/.gitkeep
dbt/target/ dbt/logs/ dbt_packages/
*.pem *.p8 *.key
__pycache__/ *.pyc
.DS_Store
Preserve source-controlled configuration files.

security_requirements.requirement: No credentials inside Kestra workflow source.
No credentials inside Python Spark jobs.
No private key material committed to the repository.
Prefer environment variables or Docker secrets where appropriate.

infrastructure_generation_prompt.startup_sequence:
docker compose up should result in the logical order:
1. kestra-postgres starts 2. kestra-postgres becomes healthy 3. Kestra starts 4. dbt-ui starts independently 5. Spark development container starts independently
Do not make dbt-ui or Spark depend on PostgreSQL.
Do not make local services depend on Snowflake being reachable merely to start their processes.
infrastructure_generation_prompt.health_and_validation:
Provide documented commands to validate the stack.
The validation procedure should prove:
docker compose config
docker compose build
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
Then validate individually:
Kestra: - UI responds - PostgreSQL connection works - /usr/data/landing is visible
dbt-ui: - UI responds - mounted dbt project is discovered - dbt --version works - dbt-snowflake is installed - dbt debug can connect when valid credentials are supplied
Spark: - java -version works - python --version works - pyspark --version or spark-submit --version works - PySpark SparkSession can start - Spark runs in local mode - Snowflake Spark connector JAR is present/discoverable
PostgreSQL: - health check becomes healthy - persistent volume survives restart

implementation_principles.principle: Prefer boring, explicit, reproducible configuration over clever abstractions.
Pin important image and dependency versions.
Do not use "latest" for production-relevant dependencies.
Do not create services merely because they are common in data-engineering tutorials.
PostgreSQL belongs to Kestra infrastructure only.
Snowflake remains the analytical warehouse and compute engine for dbt.
Spark is used because the assignment explicitly requires construction of the OBT with Spark.
Bronze should eventually preserve raw source information rather than prematurely filtering to MC1.

infrastructure_generation_prompt.non_goals:
Do NOT implement:
- Airflow - Kafka - Flink - Kubernetes - MinIO unless technically proven necessary - a Spark multi-node cluster - machine-learning training - XGBoost - feature engineering - 30-day target generation - censoring rules - production deployment - streaming ingestion - automatic Tianchi authentication/download
